newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP dip draws Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: BHP dip draws Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: Australian shares ended lower on Tuesday with selling of major resource issues BHP and CRA the main source of weakness after base metal prices continued to soften on the London Metal Exchange on Monday.

The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 8.1 points lower at 2,331.7, but off its intra-day low of 2,326.3. The December share price index closed three points down at 2,359 and at a 27.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said turnover was boosted by the debut of life office National Mutual but otherwise trading was featureless with little news to interest investors in the market.
"The weak resource sector and the National Mutual listing were the main features of the market," said Tony Russell, a dealer at Brisbane brokerage, Morgan Stockbroking.

Russell said that, despite today's fall, he expected investor sentiment would remain mostly positive for the Australian market in the near term as it mirrored Wall Street in the lead up to the U.S. presidential election.
Dealers said National Mutual shares debuted at a healthy premium as had been expected after the life office's share offer was heavily oversubscribed by institutional investors in September.
Resource major WMC was one of the most active issues on the day after the company said it would implement cost cut measures at its Kambalda nickel/gold mine in Asia.
Among the weaker industrial issues on the day were Commonwealth Bank and paper manufacturer Amcor.

Commonwealth Bank stock slipped following comments from the chairman at the bank's annual meeting in Melbourne while dealers judged that Amcor's fall was tied to continued investor concern about the outlook for international paper prices.
